hook.text: You assign the tasks. Your Agents do the work.

summary.tone: Playful, warm and confident: a character-led product demo (a cowboy-hat agent named Lucky the 'Bug Wrangler' speaking in Western idioms) on a calm off-white and Notion-blue canvas, with no narration and the story carried by on-screen text and UI.

signature_moments.description: The agent avatar is personalised via a sliding accessory carousel, named and given a profile, then the prompt is typed as a giant full-frame close-up of text with a caret before cutting back to the panel.
signature_moments.why_premium: Turns a settings form into character creation and makes typing cinematic by scaling the text to fill the frame, giving the agent personality that the rest of the film pays off.

signature_moments.description: While the dashboard page builds itself, the camera pushes into the agent panel where reasoning streams and source-result counters tick up, then pulls back as the table fills row by row.
signature_moments.why_premium: Choreographed camera moves direct attention between cause (agent reasoning) and effect (the database filling) in one continuous shot, making the AI's work legible without narration.

signature_moments.description: The single Bug Wrangler card pulls back to reveal a wall of dozens of specialised agent cards, then resolves into 'Your team of Agents are ready to work' with the avatar lineup.
signature_moments.why_premium: A single zoom-out turns one demoed agent into a scalable product promise, a satisfying scale reveal that lands the hook's claim before the CTA.

hook.evidence: Two-line bold claim stated as kinetic type with illustrated agent faces fanning out in the first 4 s; clear and on-brand, though it is a statement rather than a tension or question.

clarity.evidence: One continuous, concrete use case (create a bug dashboard, populate from sources, assign engineers, summarise bugs, update from a meeting, all complete) with each step shown as a prompt followed by its visible result; the agent status labels ('Thinking', 'Crafting', 'Adding engineers...') explain what happens between steps.

ui_showcase.evidence: Recreated Notion UI is shown at readable scale with camera push-ins, streaming agent text, counting search results, column insertion, staggered assignee fills and status pills flipping to Complete; full-window shots alternate with tight crops.

motion_polish.evidence: Varied, purposeful transitions (push, zoom_through, crossfades) and in-shot camera moves, typewriter prompts, staggered reveals and a long card-wall pull-out; consistent rhythm. Easing curves and frame-level smoothness cannot be judged from 2 fps contact sheets, so not scored 5.

sound_design.evidence: Judged from anchor audio facts, not listening: a 120.19 BPM music bed at -15.24 LUFS integrated; 58 SFX candidates, most labelled music, with a cluster of impact/swoosh hits in the opening 13 s and a chime (x031) on the assignee fill in s011; little evidence of UI SFX on later clicks and status changes. Diegetic meeting speech (w0-w7) supports the transcription moment.

vo_script_quality.evidence: No voice-over: the only speech is a short diegetic meeting line (w0-w7, 'Thank you so much to all of you.') used as source audio for the transcript in s015.

brand_consistency.evidence: Consistent off-white canvas and Notion-blue backdrop, the house line-art avatar style throughout, one sans family, and a sustained agent persona (cowboy hat, 'wrangle', 'Howdy, Partner!', 'Yeehaw') from creation to the end card and Notion logo lockup.

works_muted.evidence: There is no narration; every step is carried by on-screen prompts, agent status lines and visible UI results, so the story is fully understandable with sound off.

overall.evidence: A clear, charming, character-led feature reel with strong UI choreography and a memorable scale reveal before the CTA; held back from 5 only by unverifiable motion detail and fairly generic sound design per the audio facts.

localization_friendliness.notes: No voice-over, so no dubbing is needed, and the UI looks recreated (vector-like) so it could be re-typeset. But nearly every shot carries baked-in text (prompts, table rows, dozens of agent card names, tagline) and the persona relies on English Western idioms ('wrangle up for ya', 'Howdy, Partner!', 'Yeehaw') that need transcreation; the s015 transcript is tied to English speech.
